measured: assets-src/earth/relief/camfit.py: 171 points of the horizon (red channel, first row over the dark sky plus 45 code values, one every 16 px), a cone of half angle 90 minus dip about the nadir fitted to their rays at the terrain view's field of view by soft L1 least squares; residual rms 0.045 degrees, largest 0.134. Height is 1 / cos(dip) - 1. Heading and spot are the plan's, kept so the terrain view's Sun and sky stay as they are. Checked by assets-src/earth/place/check.py.

globe.how: The nadir of the close camera on the body and the azimuth of its view from north. Chosen so that the long island of the close image lies on the island south of the large one in the patch pyramid (1.75 degrees west and 1.65 south of the spot), with the view within 6 degrees of the azimuth of the Sun so the glint lies ahead on both sides. Checked with assets-src/earth/place/overlay.py.

plates.how: Top down gnomonic plates of the place, north up, about the point where the centre of the close frame meets the sea. Built by assets-src/earth/place/levels.py. The plate is the lay back of the approved close image where that looks at the ground steeply and its repaint where the lay back stretches, used as it is. The patch levels under it are the hold's levels with the plate laid in, and with the far cloud sheet of the place laid in where it reaches past the plate (assets-src/earth/place/ring.py). The place comes in while it is small: the first level is forced in inside earlyDeg about the centre by the share of plates.arrive. The tone is the low frequencies of what seaGain does to the hold's sea; it is added to the globe round the place by the share of the air path (plates.haze.share) and taken from the place by farness, never on cloud (tone.cloud, code values of the darkest channel) and never on grey (tone.grey: the spread of the three channels over the brightest one, none under the first value, full from the second, so the shaded side of a cloud keeps its colour), so the look changes with the eye's ray only. With that share the place is drawn as the picture it is, times gain, where the Sun stands above day; the globe's city lights, limb and shape give way by the descent ramp of look.ts, which reads the camera's height.

air.how: The air between the eye and the ground, one law for every point of the globe and of the close ground drawn on it. From the hold's height the whole column lies between and veils the sea pale and blue; near the sea almost none does. The share of the veil that is gone at a ground point is the eased step (ends) of the logarithm of the straight length from the eye to that point, in radii of the globe, from radii[0] (veil whole) to radii[1] (veil gone); it reads no time and no height of the camera, only that length, so every point in view darkens as the eye comes down and no line stands on the ground. radii[0] lies under the least length the hold and the travel reach, so their frames do not run the term; radii[1] lies over the longest length in the close camera's view (its horizon), so the surface view's sea stands whole at the change of view. What the veil takes off in all is seaGain (blue, green, red, the code value of ground that is no cloud times it), the measure of place-tone.bin against the hold's sea; the colours of place-tone.bin are no longer laid on the ground, its fourth value still weighs the place's own light. Texels that hold the unveiled sea already (the place's levels inside the plate, the close ground) are divided by the same gain by their share in the picture, so the law is one for both. Under a level the sea stands at the hold's tone (the level less place-tone.bin) times this same gain by the same length; what the level's own sea differs from that (the pale ground round the streak, the darker ring) comes with the place's own haze, by the share of the path.

glint.how: The glint of the plate as an ellipse: centre in px of the plate raster, sigma (long, short) in degrees of arc, angle of the long axis from east to north. Measured by levels.py (mend.json, glint), which stops if these values are not the glint of the plate. The glint is the Sun's light thrown back by the water toward the close camera, so it is seen only from near that direction: where the ray from the ground to the camera is seenDeg[0] degrees or more from the ray to the close camera the globe shows the plate less the glint's light, and the whole glint shows from seenDeg[1]. calm.light and calm.sea are made by levels.py: the glint's light and the calm sea under it, smooth, in code values, a square of calm.window px of the plate raster about the centre at calm.size px, laid with a soft edge of calm.feather of its width. The light is taken from water only: not from cloud (lowest channel over cloud, of 255, and red less blue under warm), and only where the plate adds as much red as green over the calm sea (glow, the green step at least floor), so reefs keep their colour; the result is never under the lower of plate and calm sea.

arrive.how: The place arrives by distance alone. For every point of the ground the globe takes the length of the eye's ray to that point times the angle one line of the reference frame takes in the lens (2 tan(vfov / 2) over the master height, so a capture at another size reads the same value): the size of one reference line on the ground, in degrees of the globe. Above footDeg[0] nothing of the place is forced in, from footDeg[1] down all of it is, and between them the share runs smoothly along the logarithm of that size. The share lays the first place level in inside earlyDeg and opens the path share below. footDeg[0] lies under the least value of the hold (0.0935 at 1829), so the hold reads 0 at every point. No height and no clock is read.

haze.how: The broad tone of the close view over the plate: the lay back of the approved close image less the plate over the lay back's cover, carried on past the cover by the recipe of mend.json veil, blurred over sigmaDeg degrees, in code values over 255 as half floats (size px over a square times plates wide on the plate's plane, red green blue and the cover, south row first), made by levels.py. The plate is the one ground at every distance; the lay back is no picture of the film any more (layBack names the work file levels.py makes it from). The globe adds the haze to the ground by the share of the air path at the ground point, and by the same share the air takes the ground's contrast where the fourth value says so (band). Past the edge of that square the value of its border goes on (the border is one value all the way round, so there is no edge on the ground). Nearer than fromDeg[0] degrees of arc to the point under the close camera the close view's ground takes none back (full from fromDeg[1]). What it takes back is a share of the texel and never more: broad is the plate smoothed as the veil is, plus the veil (the picture's own broad light at the point, same format as file, fourth value 1), and the ground gives up of each texel the smaller of the veil's unshown part and the texel times that part over broad. So a texel darker than the broad light gives up in proportion and no channel is cut at zero (the violet patch at the glint's far end, frames 1870 to 1882, was the blue channel left alone after red and green were cut).

band.how: OFF (on false, MAIL 1272, d296): the far band of the close ground is the approved picture's own texels again, the veil carries no cover (its fourth value is zero) and the close ground stands on the globe at every arc inside onGlobe.farDeg; band.py then makes the standing field alone. What follows is the law as it holds with on true. The far band of the close ground is the map, one body with what the globe shows there. Past the lay back's cover the air of the close camera's ray takes the picture's contrast as well as adding grey: with mT the air mass of that ray at the ground point (the m of share), the cover of the air is k = (1 - exp(-air (min(mT, cap of share) - 1))) times the smooth step of the arc from the point under the close camera over coverDeg and less the smooth step over backDeg, where the glow of the limb is the sea layer's own again, kept in the fourth value of the veil; the veil's colour is the old veil times (1 - k) and the air's own light. The air's light (light) is the air alone, with none of the cloud's white: it is what brings the map's open sea (light.sea, code) under the air a of the ray (the cover without the two steps) to the sea the approved picture shows between its clouds, k / a times (seen - (sea + old veil) (1 - a)), never under 0. That sea is read from the approved picture's sea layer as a law of the arc and the turn about the point under the close camera: in cells of ringDeg by turnDeg from fromDeg to toDeg, over the texels more than clearPx under the horizon, the value low per cent of a cell's texels lie under (per channel; cells with fewer than least texels do not count), in the glint, where glare[0] to glare[1] of a cell's texels are warm (warm, red less blue), the value mid per cent lie under; blurred over sigmaDeg (arc, turn); where the picture has less than trust of a turn the mean of the ring, beyond sideDeg past its sides the mean alone; past the last ring with leastTurns cells the value is held. The white of the band is the bodies that stand there (stand, wedge). Haze is by the path to the point hit: where the ray ends on a body at height z km over the sea, a standing top (stand) or a sheet of the map (sheet: km times the smooth step of the texel's darkest channel over cloud, not where it is warm), the air's cover there is 1 - (1 - k) to the power exp(-z / scaleKm) and its light less in the same share. The globe shows code (1 - share k) + share veil; the close view's sea layer holds on that band the same law at share 1, texel = map (1 - k) + veil and the tone of the open sea where the plate does not carry it, each texel the mean of lines samples down its own length on the ground, from texelDeg[0] degrees of arc on, whole from texelDeg[1], back to the approved picture's texels over backDeg, and it takes back from a texel what the law added (relief.ts thin). Made by assets-src/earth/place/band.py from the sea layer of relief/build.py and the veil of place/levels.py, after both.

share.how: The share of the close view's look at a ground point, by the path of the eye's ray through the air there: m(mu) = 1 / (mu + 0.025 exp(-11 mu)) is the air mass of a ray that leaves the ground at the cosine mu from the vertical. With mE for the eye and mT for the close camera of the approved image, the share is eased(((mE - 1) / max(kappa (min(mT, cap) - 1), floor)) to the power root, ends), times a share of the distance alone: the size of one reference line of the frame on the ground at that point (as in plates.arrive), none above footDeg[0], all from footDeg[1] down, smooth along its logarithm between. eased(t, a) runs at an even rate and rounds the first and the last part a of the way, so its rate has no step at either end; it reads the angle of the ray, never the time. Air mass minus 1 grows with the square of the angle from the vertical, so the smooth step of the ratio itself gave a ground point its whole look within about 16 frames; the root spreads that over the dive. footDeg[0] lies under the least value of the frames 1857 and 2156 (0.0417 at 1858, 0.0507 at 2156), so while the whole globe is in the frame its rim, which every eye sees flat, takes no haze. footDeg[1] lies above the largest value in the frame at the handover (0.0108 at 1919). kappa: at the first frame of the rise (2100) the eye stands higher than the close camera (0.03367 against 0.03075 of the radius) and (mE - 1) / (mT - 1) is 0.59 at its least on a 160 x 90 sample of that frame, so the share is whole there. cap is the largest value the law m gives (mu 0): the far ground takes its share last. At cap 8 it was whole on ground the eye sees less than about 15 degrees above its horizon, and the far land turned pale within two frames (1866 to 1868). So ground seen steeply has none, ground seen as flat as the close camera sees it has all. It gives the haze above, the tone of the sea round the place and the place's own light (gain, day). One value per ground point for all of them. The presence of the close view's ground on the globe comes by the distance alone (onGlobe).

plates.windows: Each level is a square window of a gnomonic raster: widthDeg is the angle the whole raster spans, raster its size in px, size the window's size in px and offset the window's centre from the raster's centre in raster px (east, north), all for the full set. The levels in under lie in the plane about the plan's spot (assets.ts), the levels in levels in the plane about centre. The windows are placed over the ground the dive and the rise look at while that level is the finest one needed (out/work/earth/place/tmp/soft.ts, option need): the camera comes down over a point 3.9 degrees south east of centre and looks north west, so the windows sit between the two. A level comes in as the texel density of what is shown under it falls from fade[1] to fade[0] texels a pixel (assets.ts). That density is the least of the pixel's footprint on the map (its short axis), counted in real texels: made is the width in px of the whole raster at which the level's picture was made, so a file enlarged past it counts by its real detail (levels 96, 48 and 24 are pictures of 2048 px enlarged twice, RECIPE.md; level 96 holds the wrap's 22.76 px a degree).

above.how: The clouds of the place as the hold sees them: one body with the close set at every height. above.py reads the place level as it is shipped (levels[0], bodies laid), takes as cloud what stand takes as cloud (stand.cloud, stand.warm), and averages the cover and the cloud's light over the texel of the globe's own cloud layer (size px over the level's window, the web set half; about 5 km a texel, the layer's own size), written like that layer: the light as coded colour times the cover, and the cover. Inside fromDeg[0] degrees of arc from the point under the close camera the globe's cloud layer shows this instead of its own specks, between fromDeg[0] and fromDeg[1] the two give way to each other on the ground, outside the layer stands as it is and the bodies of the level stand on its specks (mend.json field.density.speck). The picture rides with the cloud layer (the layer's own drift during the hold) and is read by all three readers of the layer: the cloud, the shadow it throws and the glow taken out before the bloom. Nothing in it reads the time or the camera's height. The streak of the glint is no cloud: inside streak[0] sigma of the glint's ellipse nothing counts, from streak[1] all does; and a cloud is lighter than the sea round it, by over[0] to over[1] of the code range against the mean over overDeg degrees. And a cloud is near grey: a texel whose colour is fuller than grey[0] to grey[1] of its lightest channel is the lit sea, not cloud.

wedge.how: The cover of the ground the close camera sees, one body at every height (ruling of 13:56 UTC, 25 Nov: the hold gives way there). wedge.py reads where the approved picture's sea layer shows cloud (read: lowest channel over cloud, near grey under grey, not warm; at 1 / shrink of its size, more than clearPx under the horizon), lays it back on the ground at sea level and spreads it over spreadDeg degrees; beyond the sides of the footprint the value is carried on over sideDeg degrees. The cover wanted is gain times that, at most cap, inside the envelope: from arcDeg[0] to arcDeg[1] degrees of arc from the point under the close camera it comes in, from arcDeg[2] to arcDeg[3] it runs out, and past the sides it runs out where the share of the footprint within sideDeg falls from sideShare[1] to sideShare[0]. The cover is laid as specks of the layer's own kind: a seeded field (seed) of octaves cellKm wide (each cellGain of the one before, streak times longer east to west), ranked to 0..1; a texel is speck where its rank is under the cover wanted, with the alpha rising to peak over soft of that cover, blurred over blurPx texels; its colour is the mean colour the layer (layer) holds at that alpha in the ring. The file (size px over a square of widthDeg degrees on the plate's plane, the web set half) holds the light times the cover and the cover, like the layer; the globe lays it over the layer for all three readers (cloud, shadow, glow before the bloom), riding with the layer; where the file is 0 the globe's value is the layer's to the bit. deck.py lays the same cover over the layer's before it places bodies (mend.json field.density.speck.wedge), so the bodies of the wedge stand on these specks. Nothing in it reads the time or the camera's height. gain and cap stand at a twentieth of the cover the band asks for (0.7, 0.25): the largest tried at which the hold frame 1755 in the wedge is no further from the approved hero than main is (ruling 3 of 13:56 UTC and MAIL 1191; trials in NOTES of 25 Nov, 16:42 UTC). Order of the bakes: wedge.py, deck.py, levels.py, band.py, above.py.

stand.how: The height of the map's cloud, from code. band.py reads the map as the globe shows it over times the width of the place level about the plate centre (size px, the web set half), takes as cloud what the darkest channel puts between cloud[0] and cloud[1] (code values over 255 as shares) and that is not warmer than warm (red less blue; the Sun's streak on the water is no cloud), and gives each cloud a height by its distance from its own edge: (distance over reachKm, at most 1) to the power, times lump[0] plus lump[1] times a seeded noise (cells of lumpKm kilometres, each weighted lumpGain times the one before, seed) plus bright times the cloud's brightness about its middle, at most 1, blurred over blurPx px, zero within rimPx px of the raster's edge and nearer than fromDeg degrees from the point under the close camera, where the close ground keeps its own picture. A value of 1 stands km kilometres high. One law reads it in two places, the globe's shader and the bake of the sea layer's band: the ray from the eye to the ground point is walked down from the top in steps steps, the foot of the ray at height z lies z over the sine of the ray's angle above the ground (at least graze) toward the eye, and the first height at which the field under the foot stands as high as the ray is the cloud's surface; the map is read at that foot. The shade is the map's own cloud times shade where the surface falls away from the Sun (slope times the rise of the field over slopeKm kilometres toward the Sun, on ground that stands at least bodyKm) and where another body stands between the point and the Sun (shadowSteps steps toward the Sun, soft over softKm, share shadow; the Sun no lower than sunFloor as a sine). On the globe every height is multiplied by the same share by which the place arrives (plates.arrive, the footprint of a pixel on the ground), so far off a cloud lies flat and casts nothing and the hold reads 0. The bake stands at share 1 from the close camera with the Sun of sun, the Sun in the close camera's frame at frame 2010 (tool out/work/earth/place/tmp/sun.ts). No height of the camera and no clock is read. The file holds that height and nothing else: no cloud is laid into the map for the close view, and the hold shows the map as it was.

path.how: One steady move on the globe side for the dive and for the rise. The close side is the level glide of the terrain view carried on in time; its twin is the anchor. The globe side camera stands at the anchor's height times exp(lift): lift and its rate are 0 at T, the rate eases over ease[0] frames to a constant, and over ease[1] frames into the rate of the hold (dive) or of the travel (rise). Each ease is a straight ramp of the rate with rounded ends: the rate changes by the same amount every frame, and round[0] of ease[0] (round[1] of ease[1]) is the share of the ramp at each of its two ends over which that change comes in and goes out. With k the share of the lift: the attitude goes from the anchor's to the far pose's along the one turn between them, by the same angle for every equal share of the lift. The place is the point where the anchor's view axis meets the globe; it stays on a ray of the camera that goes from the view axis to the direction in which the far pose sees the place, by k to the power hold, and the eye sits on that ray at the law's height. The handover of the dive is in its last frame and that of the rise in its first, so every frame of both is drawn from the globe side. bank rolls the view about its own axis by deg degrees times the squared sine of the turn's share, 0 at T and at the leg's end, and the turn with the roll in it still goes by the same angle for every equal share of the lift. The rise has a bank and the dive has none, so the climb is not the dive run backward. bend is the engine's bend of the surface view (terrain.bend): over its frames before the rise's T the surface view's way turns by turnDeg, about the axis acrossDeg, onto the way by which the rise takes the eye off it, so the eye's speed over its own height does not dip and does not turn back across the seam. The judged surface frame lies before the bend. land: over the last land frames of a leg the share k is the lift over its total plus (the law's end rate over the total) * land * u * u * (1 - u), with u from 0 to 1 over those frames, so the share ends with no rate of its own and the eye ends with the speed of the travel and none across it; the rise has it, the dive has none, and no frame before the last land frames reads it. rewind is the frame after T of the rise from which the spin is wound back to the state the travel starts with. pullBack (handover.rise) is the engine's option for a rise that a travel follows: the rise does not come to rest on the drift of the exit, it ends on its pose and flies speed radii a second above the drift, and the travel carries that speed on and gives it up after the seam. The far end stands back along the line of the exit by speed * over / 2 and comes out over the last over seconds. With it the law of the rise reads its end rate and the slope of that rate from the far end on the rise's own side of the seam (one sided differences over a sixteenth of a frame), and ends its last ease on that slope, so the eye neither stops at the seam nor speeds up into it.

sky.how: One sky through T. The sky of the close view (the Sun's glow just above the frame, no stars beside it) is a picture at a fixed place on the sky. On the globe side it stands at full weight below the height low[0] and the hold's sky picture at full weight above low[1]; between them (in ln height) one gives way to the other. low[0] lies just above the close camera's height and low[1] just under the height at which the dive starts and the rise ends, so the eye is between the two heights in all but the first and last few frames of each move and the stars come and go over the whole move, not within a few frames. On the path of this stop the limb stays in the frame through both moves (sky on at least 12 percent of the frame's border in the dive and 28 percent in the rise, measured at every frame on 50 points of the border), so in those frames the one sky gives way to the other in view, beside the limb, by the eye's height and not by the clock. skyFrames is longer than either segment so the engine's own share is above 0 on every frame and the weights here divide it out.

onGlobe.how: The close view's ground (the sea layer and the towers of relief.ts, the same meshes and texels the surface view draws) stands on the globe as an object of the globe world, placed by the fixed transform of place.ts, so the globe side shows the surface view's own ground and not a copy of it. It is the finest level of the ground and comes by distance alone: at each of its points (read where the close camera's ray through the texel meets the sea) the size of one reference line of the frame on the ground is taken (the eye's distance times the angle of one line in its lens) and set on the way, along its logarithm, from plates.haze.share.footDeg[0] to the size the close camera's own line has at that point. The ground's presence is eased(way / level[0], level[1]): none where the eye's line is as coarse as footDeg[0], whole when the eye has come level[0] of the way to the close camera's fineness, at an even rate between, with the first and the last part level[1] of it rounded so that the rate has no step at either end; no height and no clock is read. So every ground point takes the whole of the dive from 1858 on to arrive (to about 1889 on the far band, to about 1899 under the camera) and not the 16 to 20 frames of a fixed span of the ratio. It ends on the ground between farDeg[0] and farDeg[1] degrees of arc from the point under the close camera. With plates.haze.band off, mapDeg lies past farDeg and the sea layer leaves nothing to the globe. With it on, between mapDeg[0] and mapDeg[1] degrees the sea layer leaves the ground to the globe and from mapDeg[2] to mapDeg[3] it takes it back: on that band its texels are the map's own through the air (plates.haze.band), so the globe draws the band itself and the two are one body at the change of view; the towers stand on the band as elsewhere and take nothing back from the air, so a cloud is light from above at every height, and inside the edge of the picture's canvas over rim[0] of its width at the sides and rim[1] of its height at the near edge. Beyond the camera's own horizon it is not drawn. On the globe the mesh is not bent to the limb (look.ground.lock is off) and the push and the shimmer of the surface view stand still at the value they have at the change of view. Its look follows the same laws as the plate under it, by the share of the air path at the point (plates.haze.share): the part of the haze and of the sea's tone that the share does not show yet is taken from each texel, and its light goes from the globe's own curve of the Sun's height to the picture as it is by that share, as on the plate. The glint follows the plate's law too: where the eye does not see the Sun's mirror point the ground gives up the light its texel has over the calm sea of plates.glint (seen, glow, cloud), the texel's own light and no picture of the glint beside it; and the residue of the sea's tone (plates.tone) comes with the share as on the plate. So the ground and the plate under it differ in their detail only. In the surface view nothing is taken.

near.how: At the heights the close camera itself flies (up to its height at the change of view of the rise) the globe side draws this ground by the close view's own rule: the far band bent to the camera's limb, the picture's own light above the horizon, no end at farDeg, and the rim's feather narrowed to rim (shares of the canvas, so that it lies outside the frame there). The shell of air is not drawn there and the ball is not drawn where its ground meets the eye at less than graze (the cosine of the angle to the upright), which is the hair of ball above the picture's horizon. All of it gives way, by one smooth step of the logarithm of the eye's height, to the farDeg end, the shell and the whole ball at the height to (radii).

onGlobe.riseHow: ONE PICTURE OF A TOWER AT A TIME (MAIL 1253 item 3). The level under the ground holds every tower as the lay back shows it: flat on the sea, where the close camera's ray through its texel meets the water. The standing tower is that same texel moved up its ray. So the tower's sheet is drawn lying on the sea, on its flat picture in the level, while the ground comes (level), and one body is seen, not two side by side; then it stands up along the close camera's rays as the eye comes on: its share of its full height is the eased step (round rise[2]) of the same way of the eye to the close camera's fineness at the point, from rise[0] to rise[1]. Under it the sea layer, which has no tower in it, is whole by then, so the flat picture is gone when the tower leaves its place. No height of the camera and no clock is read; at the change of view the way is 1 and the tower stands as the close view draws it. Lying down, the far side of a tower's body is held behind its near side by behind (a share of the depth range), so that two sheets in one place are drawn in one order.
